He notes that fears of $150-$200 oil never eventuated, and those fears were driving expectations of significant rate hikes. With oil coming back down, inflation fears should recede and central banks may start cutting rates, which he sees as a positive catalyst across commodities and risk assets broadly.
quote: I think there's a lot of money currently sitting on the sidelines ready to be deployed. And I think a lot of people were waiting for this moment now probably are still waiting for the 60 days to go through. So I think as that risk diminishes, I think we'll see that risk on appetite come back into the market. You can see clearly the oil is coming back. Which means energy prices are going to come down. And I think we were seeing calls for, you know, 150 to $200 oil at times during this crisis, which never eventuated. And that sort of ratcheted up projections for, you know, central banks to increase interest rates. And the fear was there that rates are going to go up considerably. But now, you know, post that we should actually see a more balanced view and probably a view that, um, you know, rates will start, come down, coming down at some stage as inflation fears reside.

headline: CPS Capital sees space and AI tech themes as difficult to play on ASX due to listing requirements, views Nasdaq as better vehicle for that thematic
reasoning: Della-Vedova believes the space thematic is real and not overhyped, but argues the ASX makes it structurally difficult for pre-revenue tech and space companies to list via a front door listing. The ASX's listing requirements are biased toward resource companies, making it hard to bring genuine tech plays to market. He cites the example of a company (Sievert AI) that could not list on the ASX early but went to Nasdaq, raised $1 billion in debt, rose tenfold, and is now returning to the ASX. The only realistic ASX pathway for space/tech exposure is via reverse takeovers, which are hard to execute well. Della-Vedova concludes the space theme is more a Nasdaq story for now.
quote: I think what you probably find is a reluctance from the ASX to allow, uh, these type of companies come to market, uh, and it's, it's a real struggle for that. The ASX is sort of, I guess, for want of a better embrace that they don't like tech or pre revenue companies coming to market via a front door listing. Um, you know, you can very well list a piece of ground in the DRC and you know, that's fine. Uh, because they're happy being a resource, you know, dominated market. But you know, trying to bring, you know, genuine tech companies, something like a Sharon AI, for instance. Right. Couldn't get listed on the ASX early, but they go out to the Nasdaq and they raise $1 billion in debt. And they're you know, they've gone up ten times and now we're coming to the ASX. Um, you know, I think it's really difficult to play the the space angle or any sort of AI centres on the ASX just purely for the fact that the bourse makes it really difficult to list these type of companies because they've got a preset of requirements that they don't allow us to get into.

headline: CPS Capital accumulating Great Northern Minerals ahead of Nevada gold drilling in four weeks, seeing end-of-financial-year selling as a buying opportunity
reasoning: Keith highlights Great Northern Minerals as a gold explorer with a recently acquired Nevada deposit (bought out of receivership), with drilling expected to commence in approximately four weeks. Nevada is described as the world's top mining jurisdiction and the company has a tight shareholder base and cash in the bank. He expects strong upside given ongoing central bank gold accumulation and a bullish gold price outlook.

headline: CPS Capital accumulating drone defence company Foresight, which rallied from $0.20 to $0.70 and is seeking US government contracts post-Middle East conflict
reasoning: Keith highlights Foresight as a drone company that has already rallied hard from its $0.20 base to around $0.70, but he sees ongoing upside as governments globally ramp up drone procurement following the conflict. He notes that post-war, spending will shift from submarines and warships to drones, including for training purposes, and that Foresight is actively targeting US-domiciled entities including likely the US government as a revenue source. He is happy accumulating at current levels.
quote: From a defense point of view, foresight best, which rallied hard off its $0.20 sort of base and sort of touch $0.70, uh, sort of 3 or 4 days in. But, you know, that's a drone company that's seeking out increased revenue from us, uh, domiciled entities. So probably the US government, I'd say, is one of them. And I would say post war, there's going to be a lot of governments chasing down drones because, you know, before it was submarines and warships and everything, whereas now it's like, okay, actually, we need significant amounts of drones and go to take into account that even if it's just, you know, drones for training purposes, that money is going to be spent. headline: Sees end-of-financial-year selling as a tactical buying opportunity in oversold small cap stocks, with a recovery expected from August to November
reasoning: Keith argues that financial year-end selling is creating cheap entry points in genuinely good small cap companies with quality assets. He expects markets to turn back on after July 1, with August to November historically being a strong period as institutional flows return. He sees approximately one month of buying opportunity in thin, oversold names before the seasonal uplift kicks in.
quote: You know, it's probably a really good opportunity to start picking up companies which, you know, have genuinely good assets and are in the right space, that, you know, you can pick them up cheap because I think post, you know, the 1st of July, everything starts to turn back on. It won't go full swing. We sort of normally see August to November being a big swing up as people go off to Europe and whatnot and enjoy that. They're sort of European holidays. So I think, yeah, that's probably a good month or so of good buying opportunities where things are a little bit thin. But, you know, there's, there's plenty of good opportunities out there on oversold stocks.
